title: Where does a tree's weight come from?
outcome: The student will explain that plants build their bodies from air and water using light as energy.
subject: biology

concepts.title: Where does a tree's weight come from?
concepts.centralCause: Plants use light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into sugar (glucose) for growth, provided there is enough water, CO2, and suitable temperature.

cards.title: The Invisible Builder

fact.statement: Plants get the physical material to grow from carbon dioxide in the air and water from the soil.
fact.source: OpenStax Biology 2e, 8.1 Overview of Photosynthesis; 8.3 Using Light Energy to Make Organic Molecules (CC BY 4.0) — https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/8-1-overview-of-photosynthesis

hook.question: If you weigh a plant and then weigh the soil it grows in, why doesn't the soil get lighter as the plant gets heavier?
hook.predictPrompt: The soil hardly gets lighter, but the plant gets much heavier. Where do you think the plant's new stuff comes from? Guess, and say why.

cards.explanation: Plants are like tiny factories. They take in carbon dioxide (a gas) through tiny holes in their leaves called stomata and water through their roots. While minerals help, the actual 'stuff' that makes up the wood and leaves comes mostly from the air and water, not the soil.

action.instruction: Picture two identical plants with the same water, light and soil. One gets normal air, the other gets air with no carbon dioxide. Guess which one grows bigger, then compare the two.

cards.title: Light is the Engine, Not the Fuel

fact.statement: Light provides the energy for chemical reactions but does not become the physical matter of the plant.
fact.source: OpenStax Biology 2e, 8.1 Overview of Photosynthesis; 8.3 Using Light Energy to Make Organic Molecules (CC BY 4.0) — https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/8-1-overview-of-photosynthesis

hook.question: Does light actually turn into wood?
hook.predictPrompt: Plants need light. Do you think light turns into the plant's body, or does it do a different job? Guess, and say why.

cards.explanation: Think of a car: gasoline is the fuel (energy), but the car's body is made of metal. In plants, light is like the fuel. It provides the energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugar (glucose). Light itself doesn't turn into wood; it just powers the construction.

action.instruction: Picture two plants with the same water and the same air. One stands in the light, the other in total darkness. Guess which one can make new sugar, then compare.
constants: the same air with carbon dioxide

cards.title: The Sugar Factory

fact.statement: Photosynthesis is the process where plants use light to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugar (glucose) and release oxygen.
fact.source: OpenStax Biology 2e, 8.1 Overview of Photosynthesis; 8.3 Using Light Energy to Make Organic Molecules (CC BY 4.0) — https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/8-1-overview-of-photosynthesis

hook.question: What is the 'food' that plants create for themselves?
hook.predictPrompt: When a plant makes its food in the light, what do you think it lets out into the air? Guess, and say why.

cards.explanation: Photosynthesis is the name for the process of making food. The plant takes in carbon dioxide and water, uses light energy to rearrange them into sugar (glucose), and then releases oxygen as a byproduct. This sugar is the plant's primary source of energy and building material.

cards.title: The Night Shift

fact.statement: Plants respire all the time, day and night, breaking down sugars to release energy for their cells.
fact.source: OpenStax Biology 2e, 8.1 Overview of Photosynthesis; 8.3 Using Light Energy to Make Organic Molecules (CC BY 4.0) — https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/8-1-overview-of-photosynthesis

hook.question: Do plants only 'work' when the sun is shining?
hook.predictPrompt: What do you think a plant does at night, when there is no light? Guess, and say why.

cards.explanation: Plants also perform a process called respiration. Just like humans, plants need to break down food to get energy for their cells to grow and stay alive. They do this 24 hours a day. While photosynthesis makes the 'food' (sugar), respiration 'burns' that food for energy.

action.instruction: Picture a plant that stood in bright light all day and then spends the night in a dark room. Guess: do its cells still get energy in the dark? Say where it would come from.
constants: the sugar it made during the day

cards.title: The Survival Secret

fact.statement: Without light, a plant cannot make new sugar, but it can survive for a while using stored reserves.
fact.source: OpenStax Biology 2e, 8.1 Overview of Photosynthesis; 8.3 Using Light Energy to Make Organic Molecules (CC BY 4.0) — https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/8-1-overview-of-photosynthesis

hook.question: Can a plant grow in total darkness forever?
hook.predictPrompt: A potato lies in a dark cupboard. Can it grow shoots there — and could it keep growing forever? Guess, and say why.

cards.explanation: Plants can survive without light for a short time because they store extra sugar (like in a potato). This is like a pantry of food. However, for long-term growth and to make new parts, the plant eventually needs light to create new sugar. Without light, the 'pantry' eventually runs out.
